name: Switzerland, canton of Vaud

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary taxation)
paths.note: Dividends are ordinary income at the federal tariff and the Vaud barème with family quotient, capped at 30% of income for cantonal and communal tax (LICom art. 8 para. 1); a portfolio holding under 10% gets no partial taxation; gains on listed shares are tax-free for a private investor (DBG art. 16 para. 3); annual cantonal and communal wealth tax on worldwide net assets; children inherit with tax (LMSD), halved for foreigners who never worked in Switzerland (art. 36). The 60% bouclier fiscal is not modelled.

paths.name: Lump-sum taxation (imposition d'après la dépense)
paths.note: Income and wealth tax are replaced by the ordinary barème applied to a deemed expenditure of at least the highest of CHF 415,000 (which includes 15% for the wealth tax) and 7 times the rent of the home plus 10%, or the living costs (LI art. 15, DBG art. 14). No time limit in law while both spouses stay non-Swiss and do not work in Switzerland. Foreign dividends and gains are covered; inheritance follows the ordinary Vaud rules (children taxed, tax halved by LMSD art. 36).

checks.working: Inputs: a married couple with 3 minor children, no church tax, tax year 2026; taxable income far above every tariff break so the top marginal rates apply; allowances and deductions ignored as in the other recipes. Lausanne, 2026: cantonal coefficient 155% (LA 2026 art. 2), communal coefficient 78.5% (arrêté d'imposition 2025-2029), cantonal base income tax reduced by 5% (LRIPP art. 4, 2026); wealth 50M chosen so that the 60% cap does not bind (shown below). DIVIDENDS 2,000,000 taxed in full (DBG art. 20 para. 1bis not met; LI art. 23). Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2, tariff in force since 1 Jan 2026): tax at 941,400 is 108,261.00, plus 11.50 per 100 above = 11.5% of the whole amount; 2,000,000 x 11.5% = 230,000.00 (the CHF 263 per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis, 789 in all, is ignored, as are social deductions and the dividend-free parts). Vaud cantonal and communal income tax: the barème of LI art. 47 (2026 amounts, 15.5% above 291,700) with the family quotient of art. 43 (1.8 + 3 x 0.5 = 3.3 parts, the reduction capped by para. 3) gives an average rate of 13.8% (full quotient, taxable income 2,000,000 / 3.3 = 606,061) to 14.6% (capped quotient), i.e. 31.2% to 32.9% once multiplied by 0.95 x 155% + 78.5% = 225.75%; this exceeds the ceiling of LICom art. 8 para. 1 (cantonal plus communal income tax at most 30% of income), so the tax is 30% x 2,000,000 = 600,000.00. Income tax before credit 230,000.00 + 600,000.00 = 830,000.00. Flat-rate credit for the 15% treaty withholding on foreign dividends (SR 672.201): 15% x 2,000,000 = 300,000.00, below the Swiss tax on those dividends. Dividend tax after credit 530,000.00. GAINS 1,000,000: nil (DBG art. 16 para. 3; StHG art. 7 para. 4 let. b). WEALTH 50,000,000: no deductions (tax-free below 120,000 for a couple, LI art. 58); fractions below 1,000 dropped (art. 59 para. 3). Base tax of art. 59 (2026 amounts): 1,757.35 at 711,000 (ACI table 2026), plus 3.39 per mille x (50,000,000 - 711,000) = 3.39 per mille x 49,289,000 = 167,089.71, so 168,847.06; x (155% + 78.5%) = x 2.335 = 394,257.885. Burden caps (LICom art. 8): wealth tax at most 10 per mille of wealth (7.9 per mille, ok); income plus wealth tax 600,000.00 + 394,257.89 = 994,257.89 is below 60% x 2,000,000 = 1,200,000 (the 1% minimum yield, 500,000, is below the dividends), so no relief. Total 530,000.00 + 394,257.885 = 924,257.885, rounded to 924,257.89.

The tax does not depend on the actual dividends, gains or wealth (foreign income and assets are covered), only on the deemed expenditure, which this check ASSUMES to be 7 times a rent of about CHF 12,000 a month = CHF 1,000,000 (LI art. 15 para. 3 b, DBG art. 14 para. 3 b); the real base depends on rent and living costs, see open questions. Married couple with 3 children, no church tax, 2026, Lausanne. Federal (DBG art. 14 para. 4: ordinary tariff art. 36 para. 2, but without the per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis, second sentence): 108,261.00 + 11.50 x 586 (the 58,600 above 941,400, in hundreds) = 115,000.00. Cantonal base: 7 times the rent 'majorés de 10%' (LI art. 15 para. 3 b) = 1,100,000 (the 10% stands for the wealth tax; no separate wealth tax), taxed at the ordinary barème (para. 3bis) times 155% x 0.95 + 78.5% (Lausanne special tax on foreigners at 0.785, arrêté chiffre V). The barème gives an average rate of 13.7% (child reduction capped, art. 43 para. 3: rate-setting income 1,100,000 / 1.8 less 31,413 = 579,698, average 13.75%) x 225.75% = 31.0%, above the 30% ceiling of LICom art. 8 para. 1, so the tax is 30% x 1,100,000 = 330,000.00. Total 115,000.00 + 330,000.00 = 445,000.00.

The family's real case: CHF 600,000 of dividends, CHF 30M of wealth; the 60% cap binds. Lausanne 2026 (155% x 0.95 on income, 78.5% communal), couple with 3 children, no church tax. Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2): 5,692.00 at 152,400 plus 13.00 per 100 above, so 5,692.00 + 0.13 x (600,000 - 152,400) = 63,880.00 (per-child reduction of CHF 789 ignored). Cantonal and communal income tax: barème of LI art. 47 (2026 amounts) with the family quotient of art. 43 (3.3 parts, child reduction capped by para. 3). Full quotient: rate-setting income 600,000 / 3.3 = 181,818, tax by tranche 19,196.95 (10.56%), x 2.2575 on the income 600,000 = 143,012.51. Child reduction capped (income 600,000 / 1.8 - 31,413 = 301,920): tax 36,633.15 (12.13%), x 2.2575 = 164,346.67. Both are below the 30% ceiling of LICom art. 8 para. 1 (180,000). WEALTH: base tax 1,757.35 + 3.39 per mille x (30,000,000 - 711,000 = 29,289,000; 99,289.71) = 101,047.06; x 2.335 = 235,944.89 before the cap. Burden cap (LICom art. 8 para. 3): income tax plus wealth tax is at least 143,012.51 + 235,944.89 = 378,957.40, above 60% x 600,000 = 360,000 (the 1% minimum yield, 300,000, is below the dividends), so the wealth tax is cut to 360,000 less the income tax, between 195,653.33 and 216,987.49, above the floor of 3 per mille x 30,000,000 = 90,000 (para. 3ter); the 10 per mille limit (300,000) does not bind. Federal 63,880.00 + cantonal and communal income and wealth tax 360,000.00 = 423,880.00, less the credit of 15% x 600,000 = 90,000.00 (below the Swiss tax on those dividends). Total 333,880.00, whichever way the quotient is read.
checks.model_note: The engine applies a flat 11.5% federal rate to dividends, whereas the federal tariff at CHF 600,000 gives 63,880 (10.65%): the cap equalises the cantonal parts, so the engine total is 339,000 = 360,000 - 21,000 and the law's is 333,880; difference 5,120.00 = 69,000 - 63,880.

checks.working: Estate 9,000,000 to 3 children: 3,000,000 each, each child forming a stirp. The CHF 1,000,000 deduction per stirp has vanished at 1,100,000 (LMSD, successions opened from 1 Jan 2025: reduced by 1/100 per CHF 1,000 above CHF 1,000,000). Cantonal tax: direct-line barème of art. 34 LMSD (general barème), rate 3.500% for any amount from 1,302,000 (rounded down to the thousand): 3.5% x 3,000,000 = 105,000.00. Lausanne centimes on successions: 'fr. 1.00 par franc de l'Etat' (arrêté d'imposition 2025-2029, chiffre VI), so 210,000.00 per child (7% in all). The deceased are foreigners who never worked in Switzerland and the estate is wholly taxable in Vaud (no foreign share under a treaty), so the tax is reduced by half (LMSD art. 36): 105,000.00 per child. For 3 children 315,000.00.

assumptions: The family is two non-Swiss spouses who have not been Swiss tax residents for 10 years and do not work in Switzerland, so lump-sum taxation is open to them (LI art. 15 paras. 1-2; DBG art. 14). Both must qualify.

Lausanne, tax year 2026: cantonal coefficient 155%, communal 78.5%, the cantonal base income tax cut by 5% (communal coefficient taken on the base tax before that cut, which does not matter where the 30% ceiling binds), no church tax. The '12%' initiative accepted on 27 September 2026 would cut the cantonal coefficient by 12% from 2027; the projection keeps the 2026 coefficient.
The 30% ceiling on cantonal plus communal income tax (LICom art. 8 para. 1) is assumed to apply to the lump sum too, as in the ESTV calculator.

The lump-sum base is shown at CHF 1,000,000 (cantonal base CHF 1,100,000 with the 10% surcharge), the representative used for every canton. The family's actual base is the highest of CHF 415,000, 7 times the rent or rental value plus 10% and the living costs; with the prime-rent sample of CHF 9,800 a month (7 x 117,600 = CHF 823,200, +10% = CHF 905,520) the lump sum would be about CHF 390,000.

The 50% reduction of the inheritance tax (LMSD art. 36) requires that the deceased never exercised gainful activity in Switzerland and that no foreign state shares the right to tax the estate; it is applied at both deaths (years 30 and 60). A motion (25_MOT_65) asks to remove it for lump-sum taxpayers. The burden cap is modelled with income_cap in the 2022 version that the 27 September 2026 vote left in force.

A Swiss family foundation (ZGB art. 335) is not offered as a path: it is taxed as a legal entity, its distributions are taxable for the beneficiaries, and it brings no advantage over holding personally.
Treaty relief on foreign dividends is assumed to be claimed only if the control calculation stays below the lump sum; the 15% withholding is then a final cost.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the lump sum is a fixed amount per regime, but by law it is the tax on a base of at least the highest of CHF 415,000 (indexed each year), 7 times the rent plus 10% and the family's worldwide living costs (LI art. 15 para. 3; DBG art. 14 para. 3). The engine would need the base as a function of the family's spending and housing cost.

Needs an engine change: modified lump sum. Claiming treaty-reduced withholding on foreign dividends puts that income into the control calculation at the ordinary barème (LI art. 15 para. 4 f, DBG art. 14 para. 3 d); the tax is the higher of the two. The engine charges 15% on every foreign dividend and ignores it.

Needs an engine change: the '12%' initiative accepted on 27 September 2026 cuts the cantonal coefficient by 12% from 2027 (not read in the initiative text; per Berney Associes and the press), and the 2022 version of the bouclier fiscal stays unless the Grand Conseil motion of 6 October 2026 (revive the 2024 changes) is enacted, with a referendum announced. The tax file holds the 2026 rules.

The ESTV-calculator estimate used before for the lump sum (CHF 459,200) took a base of CHF 1.15M; the statute (LI art. 15 para. 3 b) adds 10% to 7 times the rent, giving CHF 445,000 on a CHF 1M rent multiple.

Whether the 30% ceiling applies to the dépense, and the 2026 amounts of the quotient cap of art. 43 para. 3 (stated for 2025: CHF 212,900 and CHF 23,600 a child), were not settled from the statute; with a full 3.3-part quotient the barème on CHF 1.1M would be about 28%, below the ceiling.
Inheritance halving (LMSD art. 36): whether the Lausanne communal surcharge is halved too (CHF 315,000 on the check) or only the cantonal part (CHF 472,500) is not confirmed.
Order of the foreign-tax credit and the 60% cap (LICom art. 8): not settled by the texts read.
